concepts.def: Demand based on need for another product.
Producing one good also produces another.
Demand greater than supply at given price.
Supply greater than demand at given price.

walkthroughs.body_html: Imagine both demand AND supply rise. Quantity definitely increases, but price is indeterminate — depends on which shift is bigger. Top-band answers always state when an outcome is uncertain and explain WHY.

Use point-explanation-application-link chains. Example: 'Cheap solar panels (point) lower production costs (explain), so EV supply shifts right (apply), raising equilibrium quantity and lowering price (link).' Repeat 2–3 times, then evaluate.

Strong answers consider time-lag (markets don't adjust instantly), magnitude (small vs large shifts), and context (luxury vs necessity good). Use words like 'however', 'in the short run', 'depends on'.

mcqs.q: Both demand AND supply for trainers increase. Which outcome is CERTAIN?
Bus journeys are typically an inferior good. If incomes rise, what happens?

free_texts.q: What term describes demand for steel because cars are wanted?
